The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: to move quickly on foot.

draft.emotion: energetic and purposeful, the feeling of moving fast to get somewhere
notes: Common expressions include 'correr atrás de' (to go after or pursue a goal) and 'correr o risco' (to run the risk).
Unlike English 'to run', 'correr' is not used for managing a business (use 'administrar' or 'gerenciar') or for machines operating (use 'funcionar').

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.

examples.text: Eu gosto de correr no parque toda manhã.
examples.translation: I like to run in the park every morning.
examples.emotion: healthy and motivated, feeling the freshness of the morning air

senses.definition: To act or move quickly because there is little time.

examples.text: Preciso correr para não perder o ônibus.
examples.translation: I need to hurry so I don't miss the bus.
examples.emotion: slightly anxious and urgent, watching the time tick away

draftBefore.emotion: energetic and purposeful, the feeling of moving fast to get somewhere
notes: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'correr' is the standard verb for moving quickly on foot. It is also used in the expression 'correr atrás de', meaning to chase after or pursue a goal.
Be careful not to confuse this with 'correr' meaning 'to run' in the sense of managing an event or business, which is less common in everyday informal speech.
